seed: No seed; whole-corpus de novo clustering of all proteins
tool: FLSHclust (own tool): locality-sensitive hashing on reduced aa alphabet, L=24 hash functions, k=12, 3 positions dropped per hash fn, 2 tolerated mismatches, MCMC-optimised hash family; 2 representatives per bucket; alignment to reps -> graph -> community detection -> greedy clustering; Python3 + PySpark
iterations: Single pass per identity level; clustering run at 90%, 50% and 30% identity (tested to 25%)
target_db: 8.8 Tbp prokaryotic genomic + metagenomic contigs from NCBI, WGS, JGI; metagenomic contigs <2 kbp excluded; 8 billion proteins; 10.2 million CRISPR arrays
curation: Clusters with N_eff>=3 only; manual curation of the ~130,000 scoring clusters
clustering: 1.3e9 clusters at 90% id; 646.4M at 50%; 499.9M at 30%; mean 2.0 non-redundant proteins per 30% cluster
downstream: HHpred pairwise-score UPGMA dendrogram of Cas7 relatives; AlphaFold2; genome editing assays
scale: 8e9 proteins clustered; benchmarks on 2-node grid, 64 CPUs, 416 GB RAM, 2 TB SSD per node; MMseqs2 on full UniRef50 (51M proteins) "required substantially more compute resources to complete within a week"
published_artifacts: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.8371343 (scripts + all redundant genomic loci); Table S1 (TSV, 38.4 MB); Data S1-S6 incl. FASTA; no HMMs or MSAs released
evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10910872 Methods summary (FLSHclust algorithm; databases; cluster counts)

seed: Each 30%-identity protein cluster as anchor
tool: Operon definition per contig; max 3000 bp from a CRISPR array defines an associated protein operon; divergent direct repeats searched within a 10 kbp window of each cluster member; gene calling by GeneMark; arrays by PILERCR, CRT, CRISPRFinder and CRONUS over six runs, deduplicated by interval
target_db: Same 8.8 Tbp corpus; 10.2M arrays
curation: Naive score = weighted fraction of non-redundant cluster members in an operon within 3 kbp of an array / N_eff; enhanced score uses searched divergent repeats; known cas genes mean naive 0.44 / enhanced 0.72; empirical cutoff enhanced >=0.35 with N_eff>=3; then manual curation
context_step: 3 kbp array proximity; 10 kbp repeat window
downstream: AlphaFold2 models; biochemical and genome-editing validation of 3 HNH systems and a candidate type VII
scale: ~130,000 of 16 million clusters with N_eff>=3 passed the cutoff; 188 previously unreported CRISPR-linked gene modules after curation
published_artifacts: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.8371343; Table S1 TSV; Tables S2-S6 XLSX
evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10910872 Methods summary (array detection, 3000 bp, scoring, cutoff)

seed: No seed; all AFDB monomer models
tool: MMseqs2 pre-clustering at 50% identity / 90% overlap, highest-pLDDT member as representative; then Foldseek cluster: E-value 0.01, structural alignment overlap 90% of both sequences, Linclust-style m=300 min-hash k-mers, k=10, ungapped diagonal pass then Gotoh-Smith-Waterman, cascaded prefilter
iterations: Cascaded clustering (prefilter -> SW -> cluster), not iterative profile search
target_db: AlphaFold DB v3: 214,684,311 structures / 214M UniProtKB sequences -> 52,327,413 MMseqs2 clusters
curation: Fragment sequences removed; median LDDT 0.77 and median TM 0.71 reported as outcomes, not thresholds
clustering: 18,661,407 structural clusters; 2,302,908 non-singleton after fragment removal (mean 13.05 proteins/cluster); 13,012,338 singletons
downstream: Dark-cluster analysis; remote structural matches to eukaryotic immune folds (gasdermin PDB 7N51, AIM2, BPI, TNFRSF4, CD4-like)
scale: 52M structures clustered in 129 h on 64 cores (~8,256 core-hours, derived); memory not reported
published_artifacts: Full cluster membership and metadata at https://cluster.foldseek.com/ and https://afdb-cluster.steineggerlab.workers.dev
evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10584675/ Methods (MMseqs2 pre-clustering; Foldseek cluster parameters; 129 h on 64 cores)

seed: Cluster representatives
tool: Foldseek vs PDB 2022-10-14 at E-value 0.1 to remove PDB-similar clusters; MMseqs2 vs Pfam with -s 7.5 --max-seqs 100000 -e 0.001; then UniProt/TrEMBL and SwissProt Pfam/TIGRFAM annotation
target_db: PDB (2022-10-14); Pfam v35.0 (Data availability says v34.0)
curation: Successive exclusion: 1,135,118 clusters with no PDB match -> 883,788 after Pfam -> 711,705 (30.9%) dark clusters
scale: 711,705 dark clusters (30.9% of non-singleton clusters)
published_artifacts: Same download sites as above

seed: 6,136,321 UniRef50 cluster representatives that have an AFDB v4 model with mean pLDDT > 90 (AFDB90)
tool: MMseqs2 release 13-45111 all-against-all; edge if match covers >=50% of both full-length sequences with E-value better than 1e-4; edge weight proportional to E-value; max 4 outbound edges per node; direction ignored
target_db: AFDB90 (6.1M UniRef50 reps); UniRef50
curation: Network reduced by asyn_lpa_communities (networkx 2.5.1); functional "brightness" from InterPro domains + UniProtKB/UniParc families + disorder + coiled-coil, names containing putative/hypothetical/uncharacterized/DUF scored zero; dark <=5% brightness, bright >=95%
clustering: 4,270,404 nodes / 10,339,158 edges -> 688,852 communities joined by 1,488,764 edges; 242,876 connected components with >=2 nodes, largest holds ~50% of AFDB90; 1,865,917 UniRef50 clusters unconnected
downstream: Component-level novelty triage; 290 components with word diversity >20% and >50 proteins used to define families; 133 new Pfam families slated for Pfam 36.0 and 37.0
scale: 6.1M-node SSN; total compute and hardware not reported (sciCORE acknowledged)
published_artifacts: Zenodo https://zenodo.org/record/8121336 (SSN + metadata, CC-BY 4.0); interactive atlas https://uniprot3d.org/atlas/AFDB90v4; code https://github.com/ProteinUniverseAtlas/AFDB90v4

seed: 94 random members of SSN component 159 (became TumE-TumA)
tool: MUSCLE v5.1 alignment, then three PSI-BLAST searches with eight rounds each over nr, split eukaryotic / archaeal / bacterial; results filtered to 95% identity; CLANS clustering at E-value 1e-10
iterations: 8 PSI-BLAST rounds per search, three searches
target_db: NCBI nr
curation: Taxon-split searches to limit one clade dominating the profile; identity filtering before clustering; CLANS map inspected manually
context_step: GCsnap v1.0.17 with a window of four flanking genes; neighbour families by MMseqs2 at E-value better than 1e-4; contexts grouped by operon_cluster_advanced with PaCMAP + DBSCAN (scikit-learn 1.2.2); only families present in >=30% of contexts kept
clustering: CLANS at 1e-10; MMseqs2 for context families
downstream: DeepFRI v1.0.0 function prediction on up to 100 AFDB v4 structures per cluster; AlphaFold-Multimer tetramer of A. tepidum WP_213381069.1 / WP_213381068.1; in vivo toxicity in E. coli BW25113 with pBAD33/pMG25
scale: One component; new toxin-antitoxin superfamily
published_artifacts: Zenodo 8121336; code repos above; AlphaFold-Multimer models not separately deposited
evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10584680 Methods, Component 159 and TumE-TumA neighbourhood analysis

seed: SSN component 6,732 representative (became PF22187 / DUF6946)
tool: Iterative HMMER v3.3 searches to build the family; confirmation with HHblits, three iterations, inclusion E-value 1e-3, against UniRef30 and PDB70; structure search with Foldseek v7.04e0ec8 in TM-align mode and DaliLite v5
target_db: UniRef30; PDB70; AFDB90Communities; PDB
curation: hmmsearch inclusion threshold default 27 bits, adjusted manually downward to find more homologues and upward to remove matches contradicted by AlphaFold2 models; clan assignment CL0236
scale: one family
published_artifacts: Pfam accessions PF21784, PF21785, PF21786 (clan CL0395) and PF22187 (clan CL0236) are the published, replayable artifacts

seed: All known anti-CRISPR proteins (100 experimentally validated Acrs) as structural seeds
tool: AlphaFold2 v2.1.2 monomer preset, 5 models per protein, best by mean pLDDT; structural comparison with US-align v20220511, default parameters; prior BLASTP filter to remove sequence-detectable homologues (>30% identity or E-value <0.1)
curation: Length <=200 aa; USEARCH clustering at 95% identity; BLASTP filter vs known Acrs; isoelectric point >7 discarded; CDD search at E-value 0.01; TM-score >=0.6 to two different known Acrs
downstream: AlphaFold2 models; in vivo Cas12a inhibition assay
scale: 43.1M proteins -> 15.0M clusters -> 14,098,963 after BLASTP filter -> 8,662,777 after CDD -> 7,178,464 final catalogue; 285,000 structures predicted; 920 candidates; 1 validated (AcrVA5Bsp)
published_artifacts: ~300,000 predicted structures on figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.24948714.v1; Supplementary Data 1-7 (xlsx); code https://github.com/EmiolaLab/ExtractGenes, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10403005

seed: Proteins lying between two defense systems 1-15 kb apart in MAGs
tool: PADLOC v1.1.0 for defense-gene calls; AlphaFold2 v2.1.2 for the 10,620 surviving proteins; US-align TM-score >0.65 against single-gene defense proteins from Vassallo et al.
curation: Window 1-15 kb between two defense systems -> 390,149 proteins from 83,926 MAGs; proteins with no CDD hit (n=28,240) and length <200 aa discarded -> 10,620; TM >0.65
downstream: AlphaFold2; phage challenge assays in vivo
scale: 10,620 structures predicted; 5 candidates tested; 1 validated (BxaP/ORF376, in a BREX/RM locus but immune on its own)
published_artifacts: figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.24948714.v1; Supplementary Data 1-7

seed: Psu protein of E. coli E101 (P4 satellites) and gpQ of phage P2 (NP_046757.1)
tool: BLASTP at E-value 1e-10 for the anchor; then the 10 downstream genes scanned by annotation for "integrase" (P4) or "replication endonuclease" (P2); genes between the two framework genes retained as the hotspot
target_db: 20,125 E. coli genomes and encoded proteins from GenBank, August 2020
search_unit: locus (genes between two conserved framework genes)
curation: Manual curation of arrangements: 121 P4 arrangements with >=5 occurrences (94.4% of loci), 310 P2 arrangements with >=10 occurrences (82% of loci); P2 arrangements containing only proteins <120 aa discarded; domain annotation by HHpred/HH-suite3 reporting Pfam matches above 80% probability; Phobius for TM and signal peptides
context_step: hotspot = region between psu and int (P4, 1-5 kb) or gpA and gpQ (P2)
clustering: MMseqs2 at coverage -c 0.6: 10,860 P4 proteins -> 541 clusters / 318 arrangements; 66,498 P2 proteins -> 846 clusters / 1,650 arrangements
downstream: Cloning and phage challenge: 18 P4 systems + canonical P4 gene set tested, 7 defended; 8 P2 systems + old-tin tested, 4 defended
scale: 5,251 P4 loci (26% of 20,125 genomes); 18,150 P2 loci; 79 P4 systems and 169 P2 systems defined
published_artifacts: Tables S1 and S5 (locus accessions and system summaries), S2 (tested systems), S3 (HHpred Pfam predictions), S6, S7 (DNA sequences and primers)
evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9122126/ STAR Methods, P4-like and P2-like detection, hotspot definition, clustering

seed: PARIS AriA/AriB components found in the hotspot
tool: MacSyFinder 1.0.2 with Pfam HMMs AAA_15 (PF13175), AAA_21 (PF13304), DUF4435 (PF14491) at score thresholds 32, 27 and 27; single-protein fusions detected with custom HMMs at thresholds 80 (AAA_15+DUF4435) and 20 (AAA_21+DUF4435)
target_db: 21,738 complete genomes from NCBI RefSeq, May 2021 (21,364 bacterial, 374 archaeal)
curation: Bit-score thresholds per profile rather than E-values; MacSyFinder co-localisation rules
downstream: census of PARIS distribution; ocr-triggered abortive infection assays
scale: 21,738 genomes scanned
published_artifacts: Custom fusion HMMs described but deposition not stated in the Methods text

seed: 1,844 CARF-only proteins taken from a published catalogue of 6,665 CARF proteins across 13,116 complete genomes
tool: Domainator (HMMER3 via PyHMMER; DIAMOND bit scores for EFI-style SSN edges); hmmscan against Pfam v36 plus CARF effector-domain profiles; largest region not covered by any domain extracted as a fragment, kept if >=50 aa
target_db: Pfam v36 + curated CARF effector profiles
curation: Fragment length >=50 aa; SSN inspection; AlphaFold2 (local ColabFold) on two random members per cluster. E-value and bit-score cutoffs not reported
clustering: Sequence similarity network of the 1,524 fragments -> 94 clusters; top 12 hold 1,391 of 1,524, largest holds 916
scale: 1,844 proteins -> 1,524 fragments -> 94 clusters
published_artifacts: Scripts and data https://github.com/nebiolabs/domainator_examples and Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10989173 / record 14056380; Supplementary Tables S1-S8; Colab notebook

seed: Psu and Phage_integrase Pfam v36 domains as framework genes
tool: Domainator: hmmsearch over genomes, extraction of the region between the two framework domains, Phmmer annotation of orthogroups plus hmmsearch of Pfam domains; PADLOC for defense calls
target_db: 2,718 E. coli genomes, about 30 GB
curation: Manual review of cluster representatives; thresholds not reported
clustering: Jaccard index of orthogroup content, network edges at Jaccard >0.7; UPGMA trees from 1 - Jaccard
downstream: Cloning of Lamassu-var (CP038295, nt 4,116,517-4,120,474) into pACYCDuet-1; 10-fold dilution spot titres
scale: 910 hotspot regions; cluster 1 has 259 hotspots; "other" clusters total 376
published_artifacts: Same repos as above, with the full command-line workflow for this case

seed: REBASE Gold Standard reference DNA methyltransferases
tool: Phmmer to find MTases in genomes, extract MTase plus four ORFs on each side; remove neighbourhoods containing a phmmer-detectable restriction endonuclease; recode remaining neighbour proteins to 3Di with ESM-2 3B; Foldseek search for Type II restriction endonucleases
target_db: High-quality GenBank prokaryotic genomes, about 366 GB
curation: Orphan-MTase filter (no sequence-detectable RE); SSN of predicted REs; manual inspection of representatives. Thresholds not reported
clustering: Sequence similarity network of predicted REs
downstream: PURExpress in vitro expression and lambda DNA digestion (Dam-methylated and unmethylated)
scale: 205,039 neighbourhoods with MTase hits -> 124,853 orphan MTases -> 2,628 contigs with putative cryptic RM systems; 2 tested, 1 active (Gba686I)
published_artifacts: Same repos as above; this is the clearest published pLM-3Di + Foldseek neighbourhood recipe

seed: Bacterial Thoeris TIR and CBASS cGAS-like immune proteins as baits
tool: AlphaFold-based structure-guided screen for proteins predicted to bind the bait and block its active site (AlphaFold2-Multimer-style pairwise prediction); predictions then tested in vivo and in vitro
target_db: More than 30 million phage proteins
curation: High-confidence predicted binding to an immune protein, with the interface over the active site; experimental validation in vivo and in vitro; crystal structure of a Thoeris TIR-inhibitor complex (PDB 9B7D) matched the prediction
clustering: not stated in the sources consulted
downstream: Crystallography; cross-kingdom tests against human and plant TIRs and human cGAS
scale: >30 million phage proteins screened; 7 families of Thoeris and CBASS inhibitors, thousands of genes
published_artifacts: PDB 9B7D; paper PDF at the author site; prediction lists not verified in the sources consulted
evidence: https://www.weizmann.ac.il/molgen/sorek/sites/molgen.sorek/files/2025-06/Yirmiya_Cell_2025.pdf (abstract and summary; Methods not retrievable in this round)

seed: 14,653 RdRP centroids clustered at 90% amino-acid identity from GenBank proteins (query DB 7.1 Mb); plus a 79.8 Mb vertebrate viral nucleotide pangenome (2,849 RefSeq sequences, 80 retroviruses removed) and a 10,101-sequence Coronaviridae pangenome at 99% UCLUST
tool: Translated search: DIAMOND v2.0.6 with --mmap-target-index --target-indexed --masking 0 --mid-sensitive -s 1 -c1 -p1 -k1 -b 0.75. Nucleotide search: bowtie2 v2.3.4.1 --very-sensitive-local
target_db: NCBI SRA: 5,686,715 runs analysed (5,780,800 targeted, 98.37% complete), 10.2 petabases; nucleotide arm 3,837,755 of 4,059,695 runs (94.5%)
search_unit: six-frame translated short reads; nucleotide reads
curation: palmscan on micro-assembled contigs with --hicon, reported FDR 0.001, to separate RdRPs from reverse transcriptases
clustering: palmprints clustered into species-like (90%), genus-like (75%) and family-like (40%) OTUs
downstream: phylogenetics; targeted re-assembly; nine new coronaviruses
scale: 11 days wall clock; peak 22,250 vCPUs (~4,300 c5.xlarge spot, ~1,300 r5.xlarge download, ~60 c5.large merge); $0.0062 per run nucleotide, $0.0042 per run translated; total $23,980; 883,502 RdRP contigs -> 140,208 sOTUs
published_artifacts: https://serratus.io (explorer, access, geo); code https://github.com/ababaian/serratus and https://github.com/serratus-bio; data s3://serratus-public/ and s3://lovelywater/

seed: 213 PAZy plastic-degrading enzyme sequences, expanded via NCBI nr and HMM filtering to 2,735,790 sequences, reduced to about 1.05 million non-redundant at 90% identity
tool: DIAMOND2 v2.1.9 with -b 0.4 --masking 0 -s 1 --sensitive; the protein set is the indexed reference and Logan contigs are streamed accession by accession as queries (inverted query/target to keep the index resident)
target_db: Logan contigs: 0.90 Pbp (0.31 PB compressed) from 26.8 million SRA accessions; unitig set 4.59 Pbp (2.18 PB compressed) from 27.3M accessions
curation: E-value < 1e-8; sensitivity stated to about 40% amino-acid identity
clustering: 90% identity reduction of the query set
scale: about 11 hours on 60,000 vCPUs per search (derived: ~660,000 vCPU-hours, ~0.73 vCPU-h per Gbp of contigs); 1.12 billion matching sequences in the main text vs 6.5 billion hits at E<1e-8 in the Methods (conflicting)
published_artifacts: Logan on the AWS Registry of Open Data, no egress charges, anonymous access; https://github.com/IndexThePlanet/Logan

seed: Arbitrary nucleotide query, >= about 1 kb
tool: Logan-Search: k-mer index, k = 31, over Logan unitigs
target_db: 1 petabyte on-disk index of about 2e15 k-mers from 23.4 million SRA accessions
curation: presence/absence per accession; no alignment
scale: about 6 minutes per 1 kb query using 12 small 4-vCPU virtual machines; index built in about 10 days on 625 Azure Standard_D32d_v5 VMs split into ~45,000 tasks
published_artifacts: Public service at logan-search.org

seed: All AFDB models
tool: Chainsaw, Merizo and UniDoc for domain boundary prediction; CATH superfamily assignment by Foldseek in several modes plus Foldclass, explicitly not the standard HMM-plus-curation CATH protocol
target_db: AlphaFold DB, more than 214 million predicted structures; TED covers over 188 million unique sequences
curation: 77% of non-redundant domains similar to known superfamilies (80% in the accepted manuscript); novel-fold candidates released as PDB files
scale: nearly 365 million domains, over 100 million more than sequence methods find; over 10,000 new structural interactions between superfamilies; 7,427 PDB files of potentially novel folds
published_artifacts: TED dataset on Zenodo (e.g. https://zenodo.org/record/13908086) with per-sequence domain assignments

seed: Single query structure (benchmarked with SCOPe40 and a 942-residue SARS-CoV-2 RdRp)
tool: Foldseek: 3Di+AA structural alphabet, k-mer prefilter with k = 6 or 7, ungapped alignments kept at >= 15 bits, local alignment weights 1.4 (aa) and 2.1 (3Di), default -s 9.5 -e 10 --max-seqs 2000; Foldseek-TM uses --alignment-mode 1 --max-seqs 4000 then TM-align; E-values from a 492-parameter neural network trained on 100,000 AFDB structures, corrected by raising to the power 0.32
target_db: SCOPe40 (11,211 structures); AlphaFoldDB v1 (365,198 models); EBI AFDB cited at 214 million structures
curation: E-value and score; a score of 51 corresponds to 50% probability of a true match
scale: SARS-CoV-2 RdRp (942 residues) vs AFDB v1: 6 s for Foldseek, 33 h for TM-align, 10 d for Dali, on an AMD EPYC 7702P 64-core CPU with 1,024 GB RAM and 64 threads; 4,000x faster than TM-align/Dali on SCOPe40, 21,000x faster than CE; sensitivity 86%, 88% and 133% of Dali, TM-align and CE
published_artifacts: Benchmark data at https://wwwuser.gwdg.de/~compbiol/foldseek; software https://foldseek.com/

seed: Protein complex (multi-chain) query
tool: Foldseek-Multimer: chain-to-chain Foldseek alignments described as superposition vectors, then clustered; prefilter for database search; Foldseek-MM-TM mode adds TM scoring
target_db: Clustered complex databases; benchmark of 931 pairs of structurally similar complexes
curation: TM-score cutoff 0.65; chain pairing agreement with US-align in over 99% of cases
scale: billions of complex pairs in 11 hours; 3-4 orders of magnitude faster than US-align; detection 97.4% (Foldseek-MM-TM) and 95.8% (Foldseek-MM) vs 97.6% for US-align; QSalign all-vs-all of about 100,000 complexes took several months on 100 threads
published_artifacts: Benchmark sets described in the paper; software in Foldseek

seed: Amino-acid sequence only
tool: ProstT5: bilingual T5 trained on 17 million AFDB predictions, translating sequence to Foldseek 3Di tokens; fast mode predicts 3Di directly from encoder embeddings via a CNN
target_db: SCOPe40 for sensitivity; proteomes for speed
curation: Foldseek E-value on predicted 3Di; Calpha refinement disabled for predictions
scale: M. jannaschii proteome (1,787 proteins): 40 min 6 s (+/- 4 min 38 s) on a MacBook Pro M1 CPU, 43.5 s (+/- 2 s) on an NVIDIA RTX A5000; ColabFold took 48 h on GPU for the same proteome and an extrapolated 112 days on the same CPU; about 10 proteins/s for the human proteome on one GPU. SCOPe40 superfamily ROC-AUC: predicted 3Di 0.45, encoder+CNN 3Di 0.47, experimental 3Di 0.49, MMseqs2 sequence search 0.06
published_artifacts: Model weights at https://huggingface.co/Rostlab/ProstT5; integrated in Foldseek createdb --prostt5-model

seed: Single protein or batch of protein queries
tool: MMseqs2-GPU: gapless prefilter on GPU (--gpu, --prefilter-mode 1), optional gpuserver for a resident database, makepaddedseqdb for the target format; iterative profile search from prior hits (PSSMs)
target_db: 6,370 queries against 30,430,281 reference sequences (3.4M UniProt plus 27M reversed); UniRef90 2022_01 (144 million proteins, 48.6 GB); AFDB50 v4 (53.6 million) for Foldseek; AlphaFold2 search space of 506 million entries; ColabFold 238 million cluster representatives
curation: ROC1 on a SCOPe-derived benchmark
scale: Throughput: 11.3 TCUPS peak on one L40S (18.4x the 2x64-core CPU), 67.5 TCUPS on eight L40S (110x); synthetic gapless 13.5 and 102 TCUPS; prior FPGA 1.7 TCUPS, prior K40 GPU 0.4 TCUPS; streaming vs in-memory 7.575/11.676 TCUPS (~65%). Single batch of 6,370 queries: 177x faster than JackHMMER, 6.4x faster than BLAST (figure caption says ~16x). Per-query time at 100,000 queries: DIAMOND 0.42 s, MMseqs2-GPU 0.37 s, MMseqs2-CPU k-mer 0.17 s. ROC1 1/2/3 iterations: MMseqs2-CPU -s 8.5 0.391/0.606/0.665, MMseqs2 gapless 0.400/0.612/0.669, JackHMMER 0.400/0.614/0.685, BLAST 0.401, PSI-BLAST 0.591 (2 it), DIAMOND ultra-sensitive 0.409. Memory 7 bytes/residue (k-mer index, up to 2 TB RAM) reduced to 1 byte/residue; database need not fit GPU memory. ~300 ms CUDA init per invocation
published_artifacts: Software at https://mmseqs.com/; benchmark query and target sets described in the paper

seed: 281 million NCBI nr sequences as queries
tool: DIAMOND v2.0.7; seed shapes per mode: fast 2 shapes of weight 10, sensitive 16 of weight 8, very-sensitive 14 of weight 7, ultra-sensitive 64 of weight 7; adaptive ranking in chunks of 400 (ext-chunk-size)
target_db: UniRef50, 37.5 million sequences (2019 release; 39 million in the HPC run)
search_unit: protein; translated for metagenomic read benchmarks
curation: AUC1 benchmark against 1.71 million SCOPe-annotated sequences; BLASTP reference AUC1 = 0.622; top 100 hits per query kept
scale: 17.77 h (ultra-sensitive) and 5.42 h (very-sensitive) on 520 Cobra nodes, 20,800 cores / 41,600 threads, 40 cores and 192 GB RAM per node; BLASTP estimated at about 2 months on the same 20,800 cores; speedups 80x (ultra-sensitive) to about 8,000x (fast) vs BLASTP, 12-15x vs MMseqs2 release 11, 6-8x vs DIAMOND v0.7.12; under 16 GB RAM in ultra-sensitive mode; output 23.1 billion alignments, about 1,100 GB uncompressed
published_artifacts: Software and the nr-vs-UniRef50 alignment protocol; alignment output not deposited

seed: No seed
tool: DIAMOND v2.8 DeepClust: ultra-fast cascaded incremental clustering
target_db: About 19 billion protein sequences defining the protein biosphere
curation: low-identity sensitivity retained down to about 20% identity (talk abstract)
downstream: AlphaFold2 MSA enhancement from the DeepClust database
scale: 19 billion sequences clustered in 18 days on 27 HPC systems; 1.7 billion clusters, 32% non-singleton; 544 million clusters represent 94% of all known proteins
published_artifacts: DeepClust database available for download per the authors
evidence: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2023.01.24.525373.full.pdf Abstract (preprint-level figures; later Nature Methods version)

seed: One profile HMM (benchmarked with Pfam queries of 7 to 2,217 residues)
tool: HMMER3 hmmsearch: MSV filter (8-bit SIMD, 16 lanes, default pass P <= 0.02), bias filter, Viterbi filter (16-bit, 8-wide, default P <= 0.001), Forward filter (default P <= 1e-5), then Forward/Backward domain definition and optimal-accuracy alignment
target_db: UniProt/SwissProt 2011_03 (516,081 sequences) for sensitivity; shuffled and TrEMBL sequences for speed
curation: Per-sequence and per-domain E-values with bias composition correction (null2)
scale: MSV is about 500x faster than a serial full Forward; Forward/Backward about 30x slower than MSV; HMMER3 is 2-3x slower than NCBI BLAST and about 3x faster than WU-BLAST, up to 140x faster than HMMER2 and about 600x faster than SAM; timings on one core of a node with eight 2.66 GHz Intel Gainestown X5550 cores and 24 GB RAM
published_artifacts: Benchmark construction described; software at hmmer.org
evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3197634/ Results and Methods; absolute Mc/s values appear only in Fig. 4 and 5 images

seed: fn3 profile HMM, M = 149 nodes
tool: hmmsearch (HMMER 3.4, Aug 2023), default options, default --cpu 2 worker threads plus a master
target_db: uniprot_sprot.fasta: 567,483 target sequences, 204,940,973 residues searched
curation: Default thresholds; observed filter pass rates MSV 20,873 (0.0368, expected 0.02), bias 17,124 (0.0302), Viterbi 2,331 (0.00411, expected 0.001), Forward 1,129 (0.00199, expected 1e-5)
scale: # CPU time: 3.67u 0.14s 00:00:03.81 Elapsed: 00:00:01.59; # Mc/sec: 19136.43. Derived: 149 x 204,940,973 = 3.054e10 cells / 3.81 s CPU = 8,014 Mc/s per core; 204,940,973 / 3.81 = 53.8 M residues/s/core at M=149. -Z and --domZ override the search-space size used for E-values. jackhmmer default maximum 5 iterations (-N), inclusion --incE 0.001 and --incdomE 0.001, stops early on convergence

seed: PSI-BLAST iterative searches from domain and full-length protein queries
tool: PSI-BLAST, 5 iterations, with and without a boundary-masking modification ("noExt") that stops already-included alignments from being extended
target_db: Pfam-derived libraries with and without partial domains
curation: Diagnosis of error types: non-homologous alignments vs homologous over-extension (HOE)
scale: 5-9% of alignments at iteration 5 are non-homologous in complete-protein searches; HOE errors occur 1.5-3x as often as non-homologous errors at iteration 5; HOE counts are underestimates because over-extensions are scored only once they cover 50% of the alignment; boundary masking improves specificity 4-8x with little sensitivity loss (hard families at iteration 5: 74.6% coverage at 1.4% FP vs 77.3% at 5% FP; random families: 89.0% at 2.0% FP vs 85.3% at 9% FP); HOE drops substantially when partial domains are removed from the library
published_artifacts: Benchmark libraries described
